second-london-equation-flux-expulsion-7a.conceptual_definition: The Second London Equation relates the curl of the supercurrent density to the applied magnetic field in a superconductor. It is a fundamental equation in the phenomenological Ginzburg-Landau theory of superconductivity, describing how magnetic fields penetrate into a superconductor.
second-london-equation-flux-expulsion-7a.intuitive_summary: This equation states that a magnetic field applied to a superconductor induces a circulating supercurrent density whose curl is proportional to the magnetic field itself.

canonical-physics-pdes-triumvirate-8b23c.title: Hamilton's Canonical Equations
canonical-physics-pdes-triumvirate-8b23c.interpretation: Hamilton's canonical equations govern the trajectory of a system through its phase space, which is spanned by the generalized coordinates $q_i$ and their conjugate momenta $p_i$. The Hamiltonian $H(q_i, p_i, t)$ represents the total energy of the system. The first equation, $\dot{q}_i = \partial H / \partial p_i$, defines the generalized velocity as the rate of change of energy with respect to momentum. The second equation, $\dot{p}_i = -\partial H / \partial q_i$, defines the generalized force as the negative rate of change of energy with respect to position. Together, these two equations form a system of $2N$ first-order equations for a system with $N$ degrees of freedom, providing a complete description of its dynamics.
canonical-physics-pdes-triumvirate-8b23c.symmetry_origin: The canonical equations are derived from the principle of least action via a Legendre transformation of the Lagrangian. This Hamiltonian formulation elegantly reveals the connection between symmetries and conservation laws through Noether's theorem. If the Hamiltonian is invariant under a continuous transformation (a symmetry), there is a corresponding conserved quantity. Specifically, time-translation invariance (if $\partial H / \partial t = 0$) implies the conservation of energy ($H$), and translational invariance in a coordinate $q_i$ (if $\partial H / \partial q_i = 0$) implies conservation of the conjugate momentum $p_i$.
canonical-physics-pdes-triumvirate-8b23c.limits_and_boundary:
1. Cyclic Coordinate: If the Hamiltonian $H$ does not explicitly depend on a generalized coordinate $q_k$ (i.e., $q_k$ is a 'cyclic' coordinate), then $\partial H / \partial q_k = 0$, which implies that its conjugate momentum is conserved, $\dot{p}_k = 0$.
2. Time-Independence: If the Hamiltonian does not explicitly depend on time, $\partial H / \partial t = 0$, then the Hamiltonian itself is a constant of motion, corresponding to the conservation of the total energy of the system.
3. Quantum Limit: In the limit where classical mechanics transitions to quantum mechanics, Hamilton's equations are replaced by the Heisenberg equation of motion for quantum operators, with the Poisson bracket being replaced by the commutator: $\frac{\mathrm{d}\hat{A}}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{1}{i\hbar}[\hat{A}, \hat{H}] + \frac{\partial \hat{A}}{\partial t}$.

H.name: Hamiltonian
H.description: The total energy of the system, expressed as a function of generalized coordinates, conjugate momenta, and time: $H(q_i, p_i, t)$.

\\partial.name: Partial Derivative Operator

canonical-physics-pdes-triumvirate-8b23c.conceptual_definition: Hamilton's equations are a pair of first-order ordinary differential equations that describe the time evolution of a physical system in phase space. They express the time derivatives of generalized coordinates and their conjugate momenta in terms of partial derivatives of the system's Hamiltonian.
canonical-physics-pdes-triumvirate-8b23c.intuitive_summary: The rate at which a system's position changes is determined by how its energy depends on its momentum, and the rate at which its momentum changes is determined by how its energy depends on its position.

dyson-series-identity-1-9a14977a-5ee794e.title: Unitary Time-Evolution Dyson Series
dyson-series-identity-1-9a14977a-5ee794e.equation: U(t, t_0) = \mathcal{T} \exp\left( -i \int_{t_0}^t H_I(t') dt' \right) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{(-i)^n}{n!} \int_{t_0}^t dt_1 \dots \int_{t_0}^t dt_n \, \mathcal{T}\{H_I(t_1) \dots H_I(t_n)\}
dyson-series-identity-1-9a14977a-5ee794e.interpretation: $\mathcal{T}$ is the time-ordering operator, ensuring that operators evaluated at later times are placed to the left. $H_I(t)$ is the interaction Hamiltonian.
dyson-series-identity-1-9a14977a-5ee794e.symmetry_origin: Derived from the integral form of the Schrödinger equation in the interaction picture.
dyson-series-identity-1-9a14977a-5ee794e.limits_and_boundary: If the interaction Hamiltonian $H_I$ is time-independent, the Dyson series simplifies to the standard matrix exponential $e^{-i H_I (t - t_0)}$.

dyson-series-identity-1-9a14977a-5ee794e.intuitive_summary: The quantum evolution of a system over time can be calculated by summing up the contributions of all possible sequences of interactions, sorted chronologically.

terrell-rotation-identity-1-76511fb1.title: Relativistic Aberration of Light
terrell-rotation-identity-1-76511fb1.interpretation: $\theta'$ is the observed angle of the light ray, $\theta$ is the angle of the ray in the emitter's rest frame, and $\beta = v/c$ is the relative velocity parameter.
terrell-rotation-identity-1-76511fb1.symmetry_origin: Lorentz boost transformations of the light-like wave four-vector.
terrell-rotation-identity-1-76511fb1.limits_and_boundary: As $\beta \to 0$, the observed angle matches the emission angle ($\theta' \to \theta$). As $\beta \to 1$, all light rays are aberration-focused forward ($\theta' \to \pi$ or $0$).

\\theta'.name: Observed Light Ray Angle
\\theta'.description: The angle of the incoming light ray in the observer's reference frame.

\\theta.description: The angle of the light ray in the emitter's reference frame.

\\beta.name: Relative Velocity Parameter
\\beta.description: The ratio of the relative velocity to the speed of light (v/c).

terrell-rotation-identity-1-76511fb1.conceptual_definition: Terrell rotation (or Penrose-Terrell rotation) is the visual phenomenon where a fast-moving object appears rotated rather than Lorentz-contracted when viewed by a single observer. This occurs because light rays emitted from different parts of the object at different times must arrive at the observer's eye simultaneously. The mathematical description of the shift in the apparent direction of incoming light rays is given by the relativistic aberration formula, relating the angle of emission $\theta$ in the object's rest frame to the observed angle $\theta'$ in the observer's frame.
terrell-rotation-identity-1-76511fb1.intuitive_summary: High-speed objects passing by an observer do not appear flattened by length contraction, but rather appear rotated due to the propagation delay of light from different parts of the object.

muon-g-2-identity-1-e4a71a72.title: Schwinger Anomalous Magnetic Moment
muon-g-2-identity-1-e4a71a72.interpretation: $a_\mu$ is the anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, and $\alpha$ is the fine-structure constant.
muon-g-2-identity-1-e4a71a72.symmetry_origin: Gauge invariance and radiative corrections in QED loop integrals.
muon-g-2-identity-1-e4a71a72.limits_and_boundary: This leading-order calculation yields $a_\mu \approx 0.0011614$. Higher-order loops and hadronic corrections are required to match the extremely precise experimental measurements.

a_\\mu.name: Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment
a_\\mu.description: The deviation of the muon's g-factor from the classical value of 2.

\\alpha.name: Fine-Structure Constant
\\alpha.description: The coupling constant characterizing the electromagnetic interaction.

\\pi.name: Pi constant
\\pi.description: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter (approx. 3.14159).

muon-g-2-identity-1-e4a71a72.conceptual_definition: In quantum electrodynamics (QED), the Schwinger anomalous magnetic moment is the leading-order (one-loop) radiative correction to the magnetic moment of a charged lepton, where the anomaly $a_\mu = (g-2)/2$ is proportional to the fine-structure constant $\alpha$.
muon-g-2-identity-1-e4a71a72.intuitive_summary: Quantum vacuum fluctuations of virtual particles cause the magnetic strength of a lepton to be slightly greater than the value of 2 predicted by Dirac's classical relativistic theory.

interstellar-extinction-identity-1-f8663.title: Cardelli-Clayton-Mathis Extinction Law

interstellar-extinction-identity-1-f8663.symmetry_origin: Empirical fitting of astronomical dust scattering observations combined with Mie scattering theory of dust grains.
interstellar-extinction-identity-1-f8663.limits_and_boundary: Valid over the wavenumber range $0.3 \, \mu$m$^{-1} \le x \le 10 \, \mu$m$^{-1}$. A typical value of $R_V$ for the diffuse interstellar medium is 3.1.

\\lambda.name: Wavelength / Linear Density
\\lambda.description: The distance between consecutive identical crests of a wave, or mass per unit length.

V.name: Electric Potential

interstellar-extinction-identity-1-f8663.conceptual_definition: The Cardelli-Clayton-Mathis (CCM) extinction law models the wavelength dependence of interstellar dust extinction from the ultraviolet to the infrared, expressing the relative extinction $A_\lambda / A_V$ in terms of site-dependent coefficients $a(x)$ and $b(x)$ as a function of inverse wavelength $x = 1/\lambda$ and the total-to-selective extinction ratio $R_V$.
interstellar-extinction-identity-1-f8663.intuitive_summary: The amount of dimming and reddening of starlight caused by cosmic dust at any wavelength can be calculated using a universal formula that depends primarily on a single parameter characterizing the average dust grain size.

exponential-expansion-identity-1-0bccdd9.limits_and_boundary: Describes the inflationary epoch of the early universe as well as the asymptotic future of our own universe, where dark energy dominates all other forms of matter and radiation.
